newsitem.title: INDIA: Tribal gunmen kill 22 Bengali Hindus in India.
newsitem.headline: Tribal gunmen kill 22 Bengali Hindus in India.

text.p: Tribal militants shot dead at least 22 Bengali Hindus sleeping in a market in remote northeastern India early on Friday, local police said.

The attackers, who were believed to belong to a separatist guerrilla group, opened fire with automatic weapons on several dozen people in the marketplace of Kalyanpur town, in Tripura state, before setting houses on fire, they said.
Seventeen people died at the scene and at least 20 were seriously wounded in the attack, which occurred at about 3 a.m. (2130 GMT), police in the state capital Agartala told Reuters by telephone.
Five of the 20 wounded later died in hospital, police said.
Officials said armed forces in the area had been placed on alert and that troops may be called in to help maintain order, officials said.
One of the houses set on fire belonged to a member of the state assembly from the ruling Communist Party of India (Marxist), they said.
Guerrillas from indigenous tribes have been fighting for a separate state in the area for the past two decades after an influx of Bengali Hindus put the tribes in the minority.
The immigrant Hindus, who came from Bangladesh to the west, now make up about three-quarters of the state's population of 2.7 million.
About 10 tribal guerrilla groups operate in the state, which shares a 839-km (521-mile) border with Bangladesh. Officials say the militants have training camps in Bangladesh.

Authorities said the attack was the deadliest instance of insurgency-related violence since 1980, when 2,000 people were killed and 25,000 houses destroyed in riots between Bengalis and tribal residents.
"Tension between tribals and Bengalis has been rising for the last three to four years," a local intelligence official told Reuters in Guwahati, capital of neighbouring Assam state.
Security forces launched searches for the guerrillas, who authorities said were believed to belong to the National Liberation Front of Tripura.
A general strike called in protest against the killings paralysed much of the state on Friday.
